title: Lightweight Federated Incremental Learning via Decoupled Replay
claim: A server-side generative model trained on privatized mixed client features enables lightweight replay, with training decoupled into separate classifier and encoder updates.
layout: 2 regions: left client-server loop, right two stacked loss panels, left-to-right
description: The left half shows a federated loop. Three clients, each drawn as a small encoder (blue) and classifier (pink) network, send features upward through hollow arrows into a 'Mixup with Differential Privacy' box. That box feeds a server CVAE icon under a cloud. Large curved dark-blue arrows labelled 'Aggregate' and 'Distribute' connect the clients and the server. A legend box covers encoder and classifier arrows and the anchor, positive and negative markers. A thick arrow labelled 'FIL scenario / Decoupled update' leads to two rounded panels on the right. The top blue panel, 'Global and Contrastive Alignment For Encoder', shows feature-space parallelograms with anchor, positive and negative points, and gives the L_feature formula. The bottom green panel, 'New Task and Feature Replay', shows the new-task network and a replay classifier, with L_task and L_replay. The total loss formula sits at the bottom. The eye goes first to the server and cloud loop.
caption: The Li-FIL Framework. Clients upload privacy-protected, mixed features to the server to train a central CVAE-based feature
abstract: Federated Incremental Learning (FIL) aims to learn streaming tasks across distributed clients without catastrophic forgetting while preserving privacy. Most existing methods mitigate forgetting by replaying historical samples, but it can pose privacy risks and incur high resource overhead, limiting deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this challenge, we propose a novel Li ghtweight F ederated I ncremental L earning framework called Li-FIL that leverages dense features synthesized by a server-side secure generator to enable efficient feature-based decoupled replay. More specifically, each client extracts high-confidence features from new tasks, enrich them via mixup, and privatize them before uploading to the server, which reduces both storage and communication overhead. A generator is deployed on the server to learn the distributions of clients and generate global features for replay. Moreover, to enable clients to better learn from these dense features, we decouple local training into classifier stabilization and encoder regularization. This design allows feature replay and alignment between new and previous features to be conducted separately and more effectively. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Li-FIL outperforms other state-of-the-art methods by up to 10.14% in terms of accuracy on both old and new tasks with superior resource efficiency.
